moat_against: ROIC history is weak: roic_proxy negative 2016-2021, 3.9% in 2022-23, 8.1% in 2024, 6.2% in 2025 — heavy R&D has not yet earned the cost of capital through a cycle
Voxzogo, the growth engine, faced its first U.S. competitor in 2026 (~90% of U.S. children remained on therapy through July 2026 — retention so far, share of new starts is the open question)
Gene therapy disappointment (Roctavian) and substitute modalities (oral/long-acting, RNA, gene editing) threaten the enzyme-therapy base

U.S. drug-pricing / IRA pressure on orphan pricing, government-order timing concentration outside the U.S. (Vimizim/Naglazymes), and post-Amicus leverage (pro forma long-term debt $4,132M at deal close)
moat_for: Orphan-drug exclusivity (7y US / 10y EU) and patent protection across eight approved rare-disease therapies; Galafold exclusivity extended to 2037 via the Amicus deal
Global rare-disease commercial infrastructure in 75+ countries — reimbursement and specialist-channel scale smaller rivals cannot replicate
Proven pricing power: gross margin 71.8-81.2% over the last decade, 77.7% in FY2025, on chronic therapies with few alternatives
Diversifying installed base: Voxzogo heading to ~$1B, Palynziq +27% YoY in Q2 2026, plus Galafold and Pombiliti+Opfolda from Amicus (combined peak potential cited at $2.6B)
moat_justification: Narrow-to-moderate moat: orphan-drug exclusivity, eight approved rare-disease therapies, a global commercial footprint in 75+ countries and ~78% gross margins give real pricing power, but measured ROIC was negative through 2021 and only 3.9% (2022-23), 8.1% (2024) and 6.2% (2025) since — below the cost of capital through most of the cycle — and the lead Voxzogo franchise now faces a U.S. competitor, so a 7+ score is not earned on the ROIC evidence.
name: BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc
one_liner: Real rare-disease franchise, moat 6/10, now genuinely cash-generative on a TTM base — but at $54.68 it does not clear 15%: weighted IRR 10.6%, weighted IV@15% $33.89; it clears 15% only below ~$33.89.
